Having the power of driving or impelling; giving an impulse; moving; impellent.

examples.text: Poor men! poor papers! We and they / Do some impulsive force obey.

glosses: Actuated by impulse or by transient feelings; inclined to make rapid decisions without due consideration.

examples.text: Americans are not libertarians in the Cato Institute sense of the word, but they are folk libertarians in this sense of impulsive behaviour, which is a feature of American life that anyone who wants to govern the United States, Democratic or Republican, has to be aware of.

glosses: Acting momentarily, or by impulse; not continuous – said of forces.
That which impels or gives an impulse; an impelling agent.

examples.text: Notwithstanding all which Motives and impulsives , Sir Thomas Overbury refused to be sent abroad , with such terms

glosses: One whose behaviour or personality is characterized by being impulsive.

examples.text: Mais, pour faire un mégalomane accompli, outre un vaniteux il faut un impulsif, un homme à emportements, une volonté de domination capable d’aller jusqu’à la tyrannie.

glosses: Persona que reacciona frecuentemente siguiendo sus impulsos inmediatos sin tomarse el tiempo para reflexionar.
